inputs.text: Mahama’s talk about policy being tied to law, culture, and “collective societal agreement” sounds less like a neutral defense of the rule of law and more like a way to make institutional control seem inevitable. Invoking his oath amid global debate over human rights could be a deliberate framing move: present the authorities as guardians of order while steering attention away from whose interests these rules serve. The statement cuts off after “I took an oath to uphold [...]”—conveniently leaving the key part unsaid.
